newsitem.title: USA: Strength in small caps push Nasdaq to new high.
newsitem.headline: Strength in small caps push Nasdaq to new high.

text.p: Nasdaq shares hit a new high Thursday as strength in small capitalization stocks offset a tepid performance in several technology issues, traders said.

The Nasdaq composite index gained 14.71 points, or 1.03 percent, to a new closing record of 1447.14, which tops the previous record of 1443.11 set on Tuesday. The Russell 2000 index, a key barometer of small capitalization stocks, added 4.05 points to a new high of 396.51.

"There's some high techs that didn't perform. In an up market like this, you'd expect more. It feels like there's some spill over of interest into the smaller stocks," said Nicholas Karos senior over-the-counter trader at Piper Jaffray. Traders pointed to gains in stocks such as Landry's Seafood Restaurants Inc, up 1-5/8 to 21-5/8, and Secure Computing Corp, up 1-5/8 to 7-1/2, as signs of growing strength in smaller issues.

Meanwhile, technology leaders such as Intel Corp and Microsoft Corp softened. Goldman Sachs said it expects Microsoft to meet Wall Street expectations for the fourth quarter, but cautioned investors not to expect a big upside. Adobe Systems Inc dropped 4-1/4 to 36 after second quarter results fell short of expectations.
